name: Simancas barracks siege memorial, Gijón
story: When the coup failed in Gijón, Colonel Antonio Pinilla and about 600 soldiers of the Simancas mountain infantry regiment shut themselves into the Simancas barracks, a former Jesuit college. Asturian militias besieged them with dynamite, artillery and aircraft, while the Nationalist cruiser Almirante Cervera fired from offshore but could not relieve them. When the building was stormed in mid-August, Pinilla radioed the cruiser to fire on his own position. Almost the entire garrison died. The Franco regime made the siege a heroic legend, and a memorial to the regiment stands near the site.
see: The 1958 Monumento a los Héroes del Simancas on the façade of the Colegio de la Inmaculada, Avenida Hermanos Felgueroso 25. It is a Francoist monument, shown here as a historical exhibit; the barracks building itself was later rebuilt.
plan: In the El Coto/La Arena area of Gijón, easy to reach on foot or by bus from the centre.

boxes.text: Status in September 2026: the Asturian government ordered the monument's removal in May 2026, but the regional high court (TSJA) suspended that order in July while the case is decided. On 1 September 2026 the national government also listed it in the catalogue of symbols contrary to democratic memory, giving its owners six months to remove it. It may be gone or covered when you visit.
